alternatives.argument: The A-page definition fixes the line parametrization x=sθ+tθ⊥ and the local negative-sign 2π Fourier convention. For f in C_c^∞, each line integral is finite because the line intersects the compact support in a bounded segment; the Fourier integrals are absolutely convergent by the stated compact-support decay and the local integrability of |ξ|^{-1} in two dimensions. The library Fourier-transform supplier fixes the same character convention. This item is a local definition and does not import a source theorem.

Fix θ and set T(s,t)=sθ+tθ⊥. This is an orientation-preserving orthogonal map with |det T|=1. The integrand f(T(s,t))e^{-2πiσs} is continuous and compactly supported, so Riemann-Fubini applies on a containing rectangle. Thus the one-dimensional transform of Rf is the integral over R² of f(T(s,t))e^{-2πiσs}. Change variables x=T(s,t); since s=x·θ, the result is ∫f(x)e^{-2πi(σθ)·x}dx=\hat f(σθ).

Under Countable Choice, Schwartz inversion applies to f and to each compactly supported smooth line profile Rf(θ,·); the Fourier/Lebesgue realization agrees with the stated compact Riemann transform. The slice theorem gives Rf(θ,x·θ)=∫\hat f(σθ)e^{2πiσx·θ}dσ. Schwartz decay and the polar-coordinate formula make the integrals absolutely convergent, so Fubini permits integration over the circle and signed frequency. The polar measure is invariant under θ↦−θ; splitting σ at zero and using this symmetry gives R*Rf(x)=2∫_{R²}\hat f(ξ)e^{2πix·ξ}|ξ|^{-1}dξ=4π|D|^{-1}f(x), by the declared multiplier. For filtered data, insert the ramp 2π|σ| into the same slice representation; the signed-frequency split and polar formula give R*|D_s|Rf(x)=4π∫\hat f(ξ)e^{2πix·ξ}dξ=4πf(x). Divide by 4π. The local theorem supplies all intermediate integrability and symmetry details in steps 1.1–5.1.

The algorithm item locally defines the exact continuous procedure: Fourier transform each complete detector profile with phase e^{-2πisσ}, multiply by 2π|σ|, inverse transform, evaluate at s=x·θ, integrate over the full polar surface measure, and multiply by 1/(4π). Its integrals are well-defined on the stated smooth compact-support input by the local Schwartz/normal-operator results. Exact recovery follows from the locally proved normal-operator theorem. The algorithm makes no claim for sampled, truncated, or noisy data.

For each row G=(0,0,1,0), the engineering DFT is X_k=e^{-2πik(2)/4}=(-1)^k, hence X=(1,−1,1,−1). The ramp samples are (0,π/2,π,π/2), so Y=(0,−π/2,π,−π/2). The inverse engineering DFT yields Q=(0,−π/4,π/2,−π/4). At x=0 the detector bin is m=2 for every one of eight directions, and the declared quadrature yields (1/(4π))(π/4)·8·(π/2)=π/4. This proves only the displayed finite computation, with no continuous accuracy claim.
